correctness.rationale: The Frobenius rank-one capture is exactly (Σ s_i c_i T_i)/(Σ c_i T_i). Exchangeability under each transposition yields f_i-f_j=-(c_i-c_j)/2 E[(T_i-T_j)^2/(DDswap)]; a weighted covariance identity gives the claimed exact 1/(2C) error gap. Ratio integrands are uniformly bounded for strictly positive filter weights, so no unproved moments are needed. Pairwise monotonicity and strictness follow termwise. Power-iteration filter c_i=s_i^(2q+1) and inverse filter c_i=1/s_i give opposite orders. Log-convex power sums prove q-monotonicity; rank-one optimal tail and pair decomposition prove the sharp factor 2. In the planar Gaussian example the polar integral equals 1/(ab), yielding expected error ab and the claimed arbitrarily large comparison. The standalone rational checker passed 6969 assertions, as finite corroboration rather than universal proof.

value.rationale: Choosing the single probe distribution for randomized range approximation at fixed expected input coordinate energy is a natural and explicitly motivated design problem in non-Gaussian randomized numerical linear algebra. The theorem classifies an entire exchangeable probe family under every power-iteration depth, proves strict extremality, identifies exactly how an inverse spectral filter reverses the optimal distribution, and quantifies an unbounded Gaussian disadvantage plus a sharp factor-two loss bound. This is a structural optimization and conditioning boundary rather than a table recomputation or a renaming of general bounds. It is consciously restricted to known singular-vector coordinates; no general-purpose algorithmic optimality is claimed.
